decisions.decision: v1 prompts 11, 12 and 13 are absorbed into S32, S33/S34 and S36, where their text stays normative.
decisions.rationale: They were never started, and v2 rebuilds the foundations they depend on (shared stage, Formula Core, Figure Kit, tokens).

decisions.decision: The v2 pack is strictly sequential: one prompt at a time, each requiring its predecessor to be done.
decisions.rationale: Requested by the maintainer so a single agent can execute each prompt completely without coordination.

decisions.decision: Recorded that CI-equivalent runs use the classic WebGLRenderer, not the node renderer's WebGL2 backend.
decisions.rationale: With --disable-blink-features=WebGPU, navigator.gpu exists but requestAdapter() is null; createRenderer throws and retries classic WebGLRenderer (programs read from info.programs; node renderers use info.memory.programs). The S01 context text and render-architecture assumptions for CI should be corrected.

decisions.decision: Added an 0xRRGGBB column to the colour-literal audit and kept per-view gpuFrameMs null where no WebGPU timestamp device exists.
decisions.rationale: F-04 quotes ~199 hex literals but grep finds 83 #hex and 230 0xRRGGBB; the column makes the discrepancy re-runnable. Per-view GPU time needs trackTimestamp at renderer construction (S04), so the harness uses a throw-away reference-scene probe, unvalidated here because WebGPU is unusable in the sandbox (Chromium 141 + SwiftShader).

decisions.decision: S01 branch was fast-forwarded onto origin/claude/eloquent-bardeen-8rt6ch, which carries the ledger and prompt pack that are not on main.
decisions.rationale: Step 1 requires the ledger; main did not contain it. The two docs-only commits ride in the S01 PR.

decisions.decision: cividis is documented as Battelle-licensed, not CC0.
decisions.rationale: The prompt calls viridis, magma and cividis CC0. The primary source (pnnl/cmaputil LICENSE, Battelle Memorial Institute) is a BSD-style licence; only mpl-colormaps (viridis, magma) is CC0. The notice is reproduced in js/design/palette-data.mjs.

decisions.decision: Machado 2009 matrices (11 severities per type) transcribed from colour-science machado2010.py (BSD-3-Clause).
decisions.rationale: The authors' page (inf.ufrgs.br) was blocked by the sandbox proxy. Severity-1.0 matrices match the published values; intermediate severities interpolate between the 0.1-step tables.

decisions.decision: Status tokens adjusted to pass ΔE00 >= 12 for normal, protan, deutan and tritan vision. Before -> after (OKLCH): established 0.78 0.10 160 -> 0.814 0.085 141.7; effective 0.78 0.10 200 -> 0.78 0.098 197.6; schematic 0.80 0.10 85 -> 0.806 0.13 89.6; conjectural 0.72 0.12 295 -> unchanged; open 0.70 0.13 25 -> 0.668 0.13 23; heuristic 0.80 0.10 85 -> 0.661 0.136 100.4.
decisions.rationale: schematic and heuristic were identical (ΔE00 0), so every pair failed. Minimal-displacement search, all six >= 4.5:1 text contrast on every surface. Existing .badge-* CSS keeps its own colours so the atlas looks the same; badges adopt --status-* later.

decisions.decision: Canvas labels below 10 px (8, 9, 9.5 px in mod-qft, mod-experiments, mod-planck, extras) keep their exact size via tokens.font.monoPx(px) instead of snapping to a type step. extras.jsx used 'var(--font-mono)' inside canvas font strings, which canvas ignores; they now resolve to the real mono family.
decisions.rationale: Moving to step -2 (10.42 px) or the 10 px floor would change pixels, against 'the atlas must look the same'. The Figure Kit (S09) replaces these labels. The extras.jsx change is the only intended pixel difference and is not captured by a baseline.

decisions.decision: ~220 frozen --pigment-* tokens preserve the exact legacy scene colours; tweaks-panel.jsx (self-contained light-theme widget at the repo root) is out of scope; float-triple three.js colours became color(srgb-linear …) tokens; bh-mobile-lab fails on the untouched base too (49,630 px).
decisions.rationale: Naming one-off shades semantically per scene is S-later work and would risk visible drift. The lint covers all of js/ (wider than the prompt's paths). The bh-mobile-lab baseline was not refreshed.

decisions.decision: compileTSL returns { node, terms } instead of a bare node carrying terms. The GPU spec uses compileTSL(...).node where the prompt writes vec4(compileTSL(...), ...).
decisions.rationale: Attaching terms to the returned node would mutate shared TSL nodes (a lone symbol returns the caller's own binding). A wrapper object is safe and the prompt requires terms to be returned.

decisions.decision: Citations were verified on 2026-10-22 once network access was opened: every DOI resolves on Crossref to the stated title, journal, volume, pages and year; arXiv physics/9905030 and 1310.1528 resolve on export.arxiv.org; NIST gives G = 6.67430(15)e-11 and Planck length 1.616255(18)e-35 m. Two locators could not be reached (Casimir 1948 on dwc.knaw.nl returned 403, the Flamm translation on Wikisource 404); both entries were removed and replaced by Bordag, Mohideen & Mostepanenko, Phys. Rep. 353, 1 (2001), doi 10.1016/S0370-1573(01)00015-1 (Crossref-verified) for Casimir, with Morris & Thorne (DOI verified) covering the Flamm embedding. Every reference now carries retrieved: 2026-10-22 and defineFormula rejects a reference without it. M_sun stays at the repo/prompt value 1.98847e30 kg; IAU 2015 nominal GM_sun / CODATA 2018 G gives 1.98841e30 (3e-5 relative), kept so the library equals js/physics.mjs to 1e-12.
decisions.rationale: Supersedes the earlier "not machine-verified" note, which was due to the build proxy blocking these hosts. Primary Casimir (1948) and Flamm (1916) papers have no DOI and no reachable open copy.

decisions.decision: Library formulas are defined once in SI with physical constants as symbols carrying their SI value; "geometric units" means binding every constant to 1 (formula.geometric). gpuSafe and the GPU spec sample geometric units by default. Mathematical pi is the literal PI node, not a symbol.
decisions.rationale: Single definition for SI wrappers and GPU use. SI evaluation of e.g. planckLength underflows float32, so GPU safety is only meaningful in geometric units; a test pins that.

decisions.decision: to-tsl maps integer powers |n| <= 8 to multiplication chains, p/q = 1/2 to sqrt and 1/3 to cbrt (tsl.cbrt, not in the prompt list), other powers to tsl.pow. lt/gt used as values compile to select(cmp, 1, 0); select requires an lt/gt condition. The webgpu spec case is annotated and skipped when no adapter exists, so the webgl2 case is the CI gate. Float render targets were readable on SwiftShader, so the HalfFloat fallback was not needed. Locally the installed Playwright wants chromium 1208 but 1194 is installed; the run used executablePath with a throw-away config (not committed).
decisions.rationale: pow() of a negative base is undefined in GLSL/WGSL and x*x matches the JS evaluator; cbrt is exported by three.tsl.js r186; the rest keeps the semantics of the JS evaluator.

decisions.decision: WebGPU is exercised locally with a Playwright Chromium 1208 (Chrome 145) downloaded to a scratch directory, launched headless-shell with --enable-unsafe-webgpu --use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader --enable-features=Vulkan,VulkanFromANGLE,DefaultANGLEVulkan --disable-gpu-sandbox. The preinstalled Chromium 141 cannot run r186 WebGPU render targets (GPUTextureViewDescriptor.swizzle is a string in r186 but 141 expects a GPUTextureComponentSwizzle), and other flag sets fail on canvas presentation ("A valid external Instance reference no longer exists", reproduced with raw WebGPU, no three.js). CI keeps WebGPU disabled, so the webgpu specs run only where an adapter exists.
decisions.rationale: S03 left the webgpu GPU case unrun; S04 needed a real CanvasTarget spike. Both now pass locally. Nothing under /opt/pw-browsers was changed.

decisions.decision: Spike result: on r186 two canvases on one WebGPURenderer, one with the cinematic pipeline (bloom, DoF, grain) and one plain, both present correctly with no validation errors. Pipelines are not shared: each view builds its own pipeline while its CanvasTarget is active (the prompt allows this).
decisions.rationale: CanvasTarget works on r186; the failure seen first was the Chromium 141 incompatibility in D-015, not CanvasTarget.

decisions.decision: Shared stage scope: opt-in per page (QGA_RENDER_OPTIONS.stage = "shared") and per scene (shared prop); pilots are AtlasStage and the two QFT field scenes. A scene with classic ShaderMaterial content or a shadow-casting light, or forceBackend webgl2, does not join the WebGPU renderer (it falls back to the WebGL2 pool or its own renderer). On WebGL2 a scene created out of view while the budget is full is parked with no context, and a scene out of view never evicts one in view; context acquisition is serialised. A scene that has its own onFrame decides whether it draws; the stage draws only views without one.
decisions.rationale: Shadows are renderer-wide state, so toggling it per view would recompile every frame. Parking and serialisation came from two defects found in testing: a victim evicted while still building crashed, and a redundant second acquisition deadlocked under a budget of 1 (regression test added).

decisions.decision: GPU time is resolved every 30 frames with renderer.resolveTimestampsAsync("render") (ms of the last renderer frame) and attributed to the view drawn last in that frame: exact with one visible view, approximate with several. The governor judges a window on GPU time only when every sample in it has one (gpuSlowMs 8, gpuFastMs 4), otherwise on CPU time, with the unchanged hysteresis and cooldown. The perf harness gained --render-option=key=value.
decisions.rationale: r186 has no per-view timestamp API. The numbers on SwiftShader (about 110 ms) are not representative of hardware.

decisions.decision: Four browser tests failed in the full run on Chromium 145: esm-runtime "non-WebGL devices" (passes alone, 2/2), smoke "bh" (software-rasterizer timing, also fails intermittently on unmodified main with the same 12 s wait), render-backends "delayed initialization plus rapid navigation" and "context loss" (both fail on unmodified main in this environment). decisions.decision: Scene3D `animated` declarations: true for the scenes that evolve while playing regardless of motion (QFT membrane, GR gravity well, scale corridor); "motion" for scenes whose animation their own code gates by the motion factor (Standard Model map, Planck descent and spin foam, RG flow, GW inspiral, QFT collision and vacuum lab, AdS and collider labs, Hawking lab, approaches); false plus invalidateKey for the GW lattice; isAnimated() for Kerr and the Planck probe glide. Under reduced motion "motion" scenes now settle on one frame and idle instead of continuing ambient shimmer. For animated={false} scenes cinematic drift does not keep them animating.
decisions.rationale: Idle static views must draw 0 frames. Ambient motion that the scene already freezes at motion 0 is exactly what reduced motion asks for; scenes with unconditional time terms (scale corridor) stay animated and are capped at 10 fps by the scheduler.

decisions.decision: View setup on the shared WebGPU renderer is exclusive: pipeline build, shader prewarm and pipeline swaps run through view.exclusive(), one at a time, with the frame loop paused. Found by scanning the views: with more than one view per renderer, scenes failed with "Destroyed texture used in a submit" / "usage includes writable usage and another usage" and fell back to static or WebGL2.
decisions.rationale: A prewarm awaits between activating its canvas target and drawing; another view's frame in that gap switches the target.

decisions.decision: The prompt says to delete the per-scene renderer path and also to keep ?stage=legacy for one release. Both cannot hold, so the per-scene path stays, reachable only through ?stage=legacy, QGA_RENDER_OPTIONS.stage = "legacy" or Scene3D shared={false}, and is to be deleted after one release. The Kerr WebGL2 GLSL path and the GR gravity well (ShaderMaterial) are served by dedicated WebGL2 renderers through the pool, as the prompt specifies.
decisions.rationale: The escape hatch is the more specific, explicit requirement.

decisions.decision: The WebGL2 backend does not reduce renderer counts (a WebGL context belongs to one canvas): the QFT view still has 4 contexts there. The 4 -> 1 target is met on WebGPU, which is the backend that can share. CI runs WebGPU disabled, so the WebGPU cases only run where an adapter exists (local, Chrome 145 SwiftShader per D-015).
decisions.rationale: Stated in the prompt's verified facts for S04; recorded so the measurement table is read correctly.

decisions.decision: The full local browser suite was not completed: a run of all 207 tests was cut off after about 108 (hours on a software rasterizer, 7 to 9 failures under load, including a11y tests that passed 25/25 when re-run alone), and the owner asked for shorter runs. Locally verified: unit tests, the shared-stage spec (webgl2 and webgpu), formula-gpu, a 9-view mount scan on both backends, and the perf comparison. The full suite, including visual baselines (none refreshed), was dispatched on the PR head as workflow run 161. The PR's own CI only runs the critical subset (qa:critical, green). On the owner's instruction the PR was merged while run 161 was still running; its result is checked after merge and any failure caused by S05 is fixed in a follow-up PR, not skipped.
decisions.rationale: Acceptance asks for the full qa:test suite on the new default. The PR CI is not that gate; stated here instead of claimed.

decisions.decision: Follow-up to S05 (PR #56, merge 2796bf29a2802ac275edc13c6544f2607ea8c2e7): the full browser suite failures left open by D-026 are fixed; the full suite run is 166 success. Scene3D build-closure invalidation: a React render owes the shared-stage scene one frame. Native WebGPU Kerr tests are skipped on the CI SwiftShader adapter (qa/lib/webgpu-adapter.mjs).
decisions.rationale: Closes the verification gap D-026 recorded; the skips are adapter-capability skips, not refreshed baselines.

decisions.decision: Two line backends instead of the node path alone: the node Line2 (lines/webgpu/Line2 + Line2NodeMaterial) and the classic Line2 (lines/Line2 + LineMaterial) are both vendored from the pinned three 0.186.1 tarball. engravedLine picks per scene build, before the scene is built: node when navigator.gpu exists and nothing forces WebGL2, classic otherwise, for scenes holding a ShaderMaterial (GR gravity well, Kerr) and for a recovery rebuild after the node renderer failed. The prompt assumed CI runs the node renderer's WebGL2 backend; the code (create-renderer.mjs) draws every scene with the classic WebGLRenderer when navigator.gpu is absent, and Line2NodeMaterial cannot run there. Option 1 of the owner's recommendation; the owner then told the agent to resolve the open points itself. The explicit-fallback contract of the native WebGPU test (a scene that leaves webgpu carries the message "webgpu initialization/compile failed: ... Retrying classic WebGL2 once") is kept: the rebuilt scene re-posts the failure that triggered the classic-line rebuild into its new diagnostics entry (found when the first CI run of PR #57 failed that assertion; verified locally with an injected compile failure: all three scenes end on webgl2 with the message).
decisions.rationale: Zero THREE.Line is only reachable with a classic implementation. Scenes are built before their renderer, and a LineMaterial (ShaderMaterial) makes a scene classic-only, so the choice cannot wait for the renderer.

decisions.decision: Engraved lines always blend and carry analytic edge coverage. Line2NodeMaterial is NoBlending and fakes transparency by sampling the opaque scene; engraved lines use framebuffer blending with three's own factors (non-premultiplied alpha, additive as SrcAlpha/One), transparent-sorted, no depth write. The quad is 1 CSS px wider than the line and edge coverage is computed from the distance to the centre line on both backends; the pipeline-facing alphaToCoverage of the node material is off (it attenuated the edge twice: 2.5 px read 2.06 px). depthFade is a TSL opacityNode on the node backend and a patch of the vendored LineMaterial shader strings (onBeforeCompile) on the classic one.
decisions.rationale: The node WebGL2 backend, a pipeline scene pass with samples 0 and the software renderer have no MSAA, so edges were aliased and widths quantised; measured widths now agree with the request to 0.13 px (0.065 px on the real GR scene).

decisions.decision: Scope of the migration. All 29 THREE.Line/LineSegments/LineBasicMaterial sites are engraved lines; GridHelper (s3dGrid, RG grid) became engravedGrid and the ArrowHelper shaft in the GR scene was swapped for an engraved shaft; Line, LineBasicMaterial, LineDashedMaterial, LineSegments and GridHelper left the THREE compatibility export (NODE_TYPES keeps the line material names). Focal curves of 2.5 px: the hardest collider track, the QFT mediator line and the two merger trails. The other scenes have no single focal line: their focal curve is a tube mesh (AdS Ryu-Takayanagi geodesic, RG separatrices, Hawking temperature rail), which scales with zoom and stays a mesh, so every line there is 1 or 1.25 px. The GR strong-field annuli stay filled meshes as the existing comment explains. Picking uses raycaster.params.Line2 = 6 px; the annotation occlusion ray is given its camera.
decisions.rationale: The prompt lists only the THREE.Line sites; hairline helpers were the remaining 1 px lines in the same scenes. Tubes are geometry, not hairlines.

decisions.decision: Fixed a shared-stage race (S05 code, js/render/stage/shared-stage.mjs attach): the view was registered after an await, so when every scene was rebuilt at once (a render-preset change) another view's detach released the renderer and attach threw 'Cannot read properties of null (reading setCanvasTarget)'. Found because the native WebGPU preset test (qa/specs/render-backends.spec.mjs, the CI step 'real WebGPU API on a software adapter') showed scenes silently falling back to WebGL2 after capture to cinematic once engraved-line setup changed the timing. Also: an empty Hawking trail field (extremal spin) and an empty foam slice set no longer throw.
decisions.rationale: A latent bug of S05 made visible by S06; fixing it is required for the S06 acceptance and benefits main.

decisions.decision: Visual baselines: only the five captures that pass on unmodified main and fail on this branch were refreshed (bh-kerr-hero, bh-mobile-lab, exp-collider-event, qft-feynman-collision, rg-flow-field-3d). Seven more captures (approaches-theory-constellation, planck-scale-foam, qft-vacuum-lab, symbols-atlas, whitepaper, gr-causal-lab-simultaneity, planck-spin-foam-lab) already fail on unmodified main on this Windows machine (font and platform drift) and were not refreshed; the share of the engraved backdrop grid in them cannot be isolated here. The two page-scope baselines were regenerated with the spec's own --update-snapshots, because qa/capture.mjs does not hide the cinema bar that the spec hides. Visual specs are skipped on CI (QGA_QA_VISUAL).
decisions.rationale: Never refresh a baseline just to make a test pass; platform drift is not a line change.

decisions.decision: Environment: the repository had no .gitattributes, so core.autocrlf=true checked vendor/three and the prompt files out as CRLF and failed test/three-vendor.test.mjs and test/plan-ledger.test.mjs on Windows before any change. A .gitattributes (* text=auto eol=lf, binaries listed) was added and the tree renormalised (no content change in the index). The pinned Playwright Chromium (v1208, Chrome 145) was installed locally to run the suite as CI does.
decisions.rationale: The base was red locally for a reason unrelated to S06; without it the vendor integrity hashes of the new addons could not be checked on Windows.

decisions.decision: Kit scenes run on the node renderer on every backend. The prompt assumed CI draws node scenes on the node renderer's WebGL2 backend; create-renderer.mjs used the classic WebGLRenderer whenever navigator.gpu was absent or no adapter existed (the same gap as D-028). createRenderer now attempts "node-webgl2" (WebGPURenderer({ forceWebGL: true })) for a scene holding a kit material (userData.qgaNodeKit): after WebGPU when an adapter exists, instead of it when WebGPU is absent or WebGL2 is forced, never the classic renderer; the shared stage (forceBackend "webgpu") still takes WebGPU or nothing. Scene3D gained nodeKit (node engraved lines through requireNode, no classic recovery). Scenes whose only node-only content is engraved lines keep their D-028 classic recovery.
decisions.rationale: Without it a node-material GR scene cannot be drawn at all on browsers without WebGPU, which is where CI runs.

decisions.decision: Acceptance "no ShaderMaterial outside kerr-material.mjs" is met except js/visualizations/gw/gw-runtime.mjs (2 sites): the WebGL2 twin of the WebGPU compute lattice of the GW instrument. perf:audit ShaderMaterial sites 13 -> 8 (mod-gr.jsx 3 and the three-runtime.mjs compatibility export 2 removed); test/material-kit.test.mjs pins the allowlist to those two files.
decisions.rationale: The step list names the mod-gr.jsx sites; S26 ("a GPU spacetime field") replaces the GW lattice and its twin. Porting it here would widen S07 into the GW instrument and its audio-synchronised tests.

decisions.decision: The blackbody table holds blackbodyToSrgb(T).linearRgb, the peak-normalised linear triple that function returns, not a unit-luminance triple; brightness is the radiance factor. The table is half float (DataUtils.toHalfFloat) so linear filtering works on every backend without OES_texture_float_linear; the 1e-6 equality is asserted on the float32 table, the texture is within 1e-3 of it.
decisions.rationale: One definition of the colour on CPU and GPU: the test compares against the existing function rather than a second normalisation.

decisions.decision: Registered the compatibility lights (AmbientLight, DirectionalLight, PointLight of three-runtime.mjs) with every node renderer. They are subclasses and the node library looks a light node up by exact constructor, so every compatibility light was ignored ("Light node not found") and lit meshes rendered unlit on node renderers. Found when the GR scene moved to the node renderer. Also fixed in the move: two GR formula readouts read an undefined GR_BODIES, and the starfield and dust used Math.random (now seededRng; Math.random sites 35 -> 27). Visual changes of the GR scene (D-038): tone mapping now applies to the star, well and starfield (they bypassed it as ShaderMaterials), the well ramp uses design tokens, points are soft-disc sprites; the visual specs are local-only and were not refreshed here.
decisions.rationale: Correctness of the node path the S07 scene now depends on.

decisions.decision: On the node renderer's WebGL2 backend (transform feedback) a kernel reads its own buffers through the variable it writes, so a read placed after an assignment sees the new value, and two kernels (init and update) over the same buffers do not stay in step with each other. The particle kit therefore runs init and update as ONE kernel selected by a uniform, copies the previous state into locals first, and assigns every buffer exactly once. init and update are builders that return the new state instead of assigning.
decisions.rationale: Verified against r186 by the GPU-vs-CPU readback: with separate kernels or late reads a re-initialised run diverged by up to 4 units.

decisions.decision: Each particle system's kernel carries a per-system serial constant that changes its source and not its maths. r186 caches a compiled program by source and the program keeps the attribute list of the first kernel that produced it, so on the WebGL2 backend a second system with identical source computed into the first system's buffers and left its own untouched; a lab re-mount would have drawn stale buffers.
decisions.rationale: Found by the determinism test (a second system read back empty). Without it every rebuilt Hawking, RG, QFT or backdrop scene would break after its first mount.

decisions.decision: Tolerances of the GPU-vs-CPU test: 1e-4 on positions, velocities, ages and attributes after 60 fixed steps (the prompt's bound; Hawking and tracer positions agree to 1e-6, the reference system exactly), 5e-4 on the Hawking opacity (pow(sin(.), 0.7)) and 1e-3 on the QFT crest heights (24 cosines of arguments up to ~100 rad); the crest mask matches exactly. The reference behaviour uses a normalised cube sample instead of sin and cos for its direction.
decisions.rationale: sin, cos and pow are accurate to about 1e-4 on the software rasteriser CI runs; the bound is the platform's, not the algorithm's.

decisions.decision: Scope of the migrations. Moved to GPU systems: atlas backdrop stars (static seeded buffer, vertex-stage twinkle), Hawking pair field (the engraved trail segments became tail dots of the same system), RG flow tracers (a resampled float table, two texel loads), QFT crest markers (the closed-form mode sum), collider towers (vertex-stage rise about each tower's base) and every THREE.Points left in those scenes (one pixel on both node backends). NOT moved: the QFT waterfall surface (a mesh with a CPU ring buffer; S14 replaces it with the GPU lattice), the GW lattice (its needsUpdate sites upload the signal once per signal, never per frame, and its WebGL2 twin already deforms in the vertex stage; S26 replaces it), engraved-lines.mjs and the mod-planck, mod-experiments, mod-qft and extras canvases (line and 2D upload paths outside the six listed systems). F-27 therefore stays open.
decisions.rationale: Each of those is either not a particle system or is rewritten by a later prompt in the pack; moving it here would have duplicated that work. needsUpdate sites 38 -> 33.

decisions.decision: Every scene holding a GPU system or kit material is a kit scene (Scene3D nodeKit): the atlas backdrop, the Hawking, RG, QFT and collider labs now run on the node renderer (WebGPU, or its WebGL2 backend), with the node engraved lines and no classic fallback. Scene3D gained prepare(renderer) and compute(renderer, dt); compute runs on the session's live renderer only, a scene parked by the WebGL2 pool is not prepared until it has one, and a system seeds itself again when the renderer changes.
decisions.rationale: The three systems that reach the renderer through the session must survive pool eviction and restore; both defects were found by the shared-stage budget specs.

decisions.decision: Visual changes (visual baselines are local-only and were not refreshed): Hawking trails are dotted tails instead of engraved lines; the backdrop stars follow the shared glow profile and a slightly different twinkle (colour = base colour x (0.6 + 0.4 tw)); the QFT, collider, RG and Hawking scenes are now tone-mapped by the node pipeline; the QFT crest sprites show every crest rather than the first 24. Perf (docs/audit/s08-before.json vs s08-after.json, software rasteriser, desktop, p95 CPU frame ms): overview 316.6 -> 350.0, qft 350.0 -> 316.7, rg 333.4 -> 350.1, bh 766.5 -> 766.7, exp 283.3 -> 349.9: within the noise of a rasteriser-bound frame (quantised at ~16.7 ms steps); no hardware measurement was possible here.
decisions.rationale: Recorded, not hidden: the prompt asks for p95 deltas per migrated view, and on this platform they are not distinguishable from noise.
